chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Jamilah, from Jabir, from Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Jibra'il came to me while I was between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and said: 'O Muhammad! Blessed is anyone from your Ummah who says: There is no god but Allah, Unique, with sincerity.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: Safa and Marwah (the hills in Mecca)
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for sincere monotheism according to the hadith of Jibra'il at Safa and Marwah?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Tawhid*, this hadith links the declaration of pure monotheism (*tawhid*) to the sacred geography of the Hajj, specifically between Safa and Marwah, emphasizing the spiritual weight of sincerity (*ikhlas*). It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Prophet’s direct encounter with Jibra'il in this holy space validates the eternal reward for those who uphold the core tenet of faith with genuine devotion.
